text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Fruit and vegetables more expensive than before Finland joined the EU in 1995. Prices of vegetables rose 16 percent and prices of fruit rose four percent this year.
- Finland's spending on education among the highest in the OECD countries, recent statistics show.
- Violence and drug-related crimes increasingly common among women prisoners.
- Forestry sector has lost 80,000 jobs in the last 15 years.
- Enso, Metsa-Serla's Metsa-Botnia and UPM-Kymmene plan to raise pulp prices at the start of next year, following similar announcements from rivals.

- Kemira plans to follow DuPont's example and lift its titanium dioxide price at the start of next year in the U.S. and Europe, with a corresponding improvement in its titanium dioxide division's outlook if the hikes succeed.
- Finland plans proposal on forestry certification by March next year.
- China received more subsidised finance from Finland than any other country between 1988 and 1995, when the value of Finland's credit subsidy to China totalled 600 million markka.
- Information technology group KT-Tietokeskus will broaden its ownership base with a share issue to institutions ahead of Christmas but has not decided whether to go public.
- Women who have had abortion are six times more likely to commit suicide than others.

- Opposition has not given up its fight against reducing the number of regions to five from 11 - it is trying to close the government's 11-seat margin in the second reading by Wednesday's third reading in parliament.
- Energy tax proposal advances in parliament according to plan.
